title: Maintaining IV Patency Throughout Pharmacokinetic Studies Through a Needle-Free Blood Draw Device.
abstract: 8 8 9 Pharmacokinetic (PK) studies require temporally precise measurements of drug concentrations in biological matrices, most commonly whole blood or plasma. However, repeated venous sampling may increase participant burden and complicate PK-intensive study designs. Needle-free blood collection devices that access peripheral intravenous (IV) catheters may provide an alternative approach to repeated venipuncture while maintaining sampling schedules and specimen quality. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility of integrating the PIVO Pro needle-free blood collection device into a PK-intensive human laboratory study of inhaled Δ-tetrahydrocannabinol (Δ-THC), Δ-THC, and placebo. Participants completed a screening visit and three dosing visits conducted in a university research facility equipped with a full-scale driving simulator. During each dosing visit, venous blood samples were collected at nine time points over approximately 8 h through an indwelling peripheral IV catheter using the PIVO device. All participants reported that study procedures, including blood collection, were acceptable. Approximately 40% of vascular access sites required replacement, most commonly within the first hour and typically associated with poor initial blood return. Despite slower flow compared with standard venipuncture, sampling was generally sufficient to maintain the PK sampling schedule. One mild adverse event related to vascular access (localized bruising) was observed. These findings demonstrate the operational feasibility of needle-free blood collection through indwelling IV catheters in a PK-intensive research protocol conducted outside a traditional clinical research unit. Further studies are warranted to compare analytical performance and access durability relative to conventional venous sampling approaches.

title: Performance of Western HA-VTE risk models in East Asian populations: a prospective multicenter study.
abstract: Hospital-associated venous thromboembolism (HA-VTE) causes significant morbidity, but risk prediction models are inconsistently validated, especially in non-Western populations. We prospectively validated 5 HA-VTE risk scores (Caprini, Padua, IMPROVE [International Medical Prevention Registry on Venous Thromboembolism], Kucher, and Intermountain) in a prospective multicenter cohort of 2948 adult inpatients from 17 Chinese hospitals. Symptomatic VTE events were recorded through 3 months of follow-up. The 90-day HA-VTE incidence was 2.54%. All 5 models showed moderate discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC], 0.726-0.759). Caprini, Padua, and Intermountain models did not differ significantly (DeLong test, P> .05). Caprini had the highest sensitivity (0.83) but classified 42.6% of patients as being at high risk. Padua and Intermountain favored specificity (0.75-0.81) with lower sensitivity (0.64-0.67). Clinical model selection should align with specific balances between sensitivity and utility. In surgical inpatients, Caprini performed best (AUC, 0.804; sensitivity, 0.90; negative predictive value, 1.00), although its more than 40 input variables limit practical use. Calibration was generally acceptable. Performance varied across subgroups. The prophylaxis subgroup showed attenuated performance, with reduced discrimination (eg, Caprini AUC decreased to 0.682) and less stable calibration. Western HA-VTE models have moderate predictive value in East Asian inpatient populations. Performance differs across subgroups. Local recalibration and development of simpler, population-specific scores are needed.

title: Use of a central venous catheter as vascular access at the start of a regular hemodialysis program: impact on mortality over 2 years.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The recommended access for starting chronic hemodialysis (HD) is an arteriovenous fistula (AVF), but a (CVC) continues to be frequently used. Worldwide, its use has been associated with higher mortality, but data from Brazil are lacking. METHODS: Analytical, observational, and retrospective cohort study that aimed at analyzing the data available in the Brazilian Monthly Dialysis Registry database from Jan/2011 to Dec/2023. Using data from this registry, we evaluated the frequency of CVC use (regardless of whether tunneled or non-tunneled) at the start of HD across 13 years and assessed its impact on all-cause mortality over 2 years. RESULTS: We studied 10,182 patients. The mean age was 59 (47-69) years; 59% were male, and 33% had diabetes. CVC use at HD entry increased substantially in the last 10 years. The 2-year mortality rates for CVC and primary AVF/graft users were 20% and 9%, respectively, P < 0.001. In the fully adjusted multivariate model, the use of CVC persisted significantly associated with mortality (HR 1.69, 95%CI 1.23-2.25, P=0.001). Other variables directly associated with mortality were age (HR 1.04, 95%CI 1.03-1.05, P=0.001), and serum ferritin (HR 1.18, 95%CI 1.06-1.30, P=0.002). Serum albumin (HR 0.86, 95%CI 0.84-0.88, P<0.001) and URR (HR 0.97, 95%CI 0.96-0.97, P<0.001) emerged as protective factors. CONCLUSIONS: CVC use was associated with a 1.69-fold increased risk of 2-year mortality. The increasing use of CVCs in Brazil is concerning and highlights the need for public health strategies promoting timely permanent vascular access before HD initiation.

title: Electrosurgical septotomy across the full spectrum of aortic dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Transcatheter electrosurgical septotomy divides the dissection membrane to reconstitute a single aortic lumen. Reported experience is largely confined to chronic post-dissection aneurysms. We assessed the technique across the full spectrum of descending aortic dissection, including stand-alone treatment of malperfusion. METHODS: Retrospective intention-to-treat analysis of 21 consecutive patients scheduled for septotomy between June 2022 and May 2026. The membrane was crossed by needle re-entry and divided with an electrified through-and-through guidewire at 40-60 W under fluoroscopy, without routine intravascular ultrasound or image fusion. A perfused-lumen index (perfused lumen divided by total aortic diameter) was measured before and after the procedure. RESULTS: Septotomy was performed in 20 of 21 patients (technical success 95% on an intention-to-treat basis). Indications were landing-zone preparation (57%), malperfusion (33%), preparation for open repair and true-lumen collapse. Malperfusion resolved in all 7 patients treated for that indication, and the perfused-lumen index rose from a median of 0.16 to 0.98 (18 patients, P < 0.001). There was no stroke, spinal cord ischaemia or retrograde type A dissection. Thirty-day, in-hospital and overall mortality were 10%, 14% and 19%, with one fatal delayed aortic rupture and no intraprocedural death. Three unplanned reinterventions occurred; median follow-up was 5.1 months. CONCLUSIONS: Electrosurgical septotomy was feasible across the full spectrum of aortic dissection and, in selected patients, as stand-alone treatment for malperfusion, using standard electrosurgical equipment. Given the small heterogeneous cohort and short follow-up, these findings demonstrate feasibility rather than durability.

title: Adiposity and the risk of aortic dissection incidence and mortality: results from the UK Biobank, the J-SHC study and a meta-analysis of cohort studies.
abstract: trend trend trend trend trend trend trend trend trend trend 2 2 2 2 Few studies have investigated the association between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection and data is lacking on adiposity measures other than body mass index (BMI). We analyzed the association between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection in the UK Biobank, and the Japan Specific Health Checkups (J-SHC) Study, and conducted a meta-analysis of cohort studies to clarify the associations between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection. The analytical cohorts included 496,255 participants in the UK Biobank and 630,841 participants in the J-SHC Study. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to analyze associations between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection. PubMed and Embase were searched for relevant studies up to February 27, 2026. Random effects models were used to calculate summary relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the association between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection. In the UK Biobank and J-SHC, there were 371 and 105 aortic dissections during 12.3 and 4 years follow-up, respectively. In the UK Biobank, positive associations (HRs, 95% CIs) were observed between high BMI (1.54, 1.01-2.37, p=0.01), waist circumference (1.82, 1.27-2.60, p=0.001), hip circumference (1.77, 1.25-2.50, p<0.001), waist-to-height ratio (1.88, 1.30-2.70, p=0.10), and fat mass (1.36, 0.97-1.91, p=0.02) and aortic dissection risk, but no clear association was observed for waist-to-hip ratio (1.28, 0.90-1.81, p=0.08) and body fat percentage (1.09, 0.77-1.54, p=0.53). In the J-SHC Study, higher BMI (2.36, 0.98-4.84, p=0.018), waist circumference (2.26, 1.18-4.60, p=0.003), and waist-to-height ratio (2.61, 1.27-5.92, p=0.009) were positively associated with aortic dissection mortality. Five cohort studies were included in the meta-analysis on BMI and aortic dissection (2007 cases and 4,962,288 participants). The summary RR per 5 kg/mincrement in BMI was 1.09 (1.00-1.20, I = 43%), per 10 cm increment in waist circumference was 1.21 (1.05-1.40, I = 50%, n = 2), and per 0.1 unit increment in waist-to-height ratio was 1.32 (1.08-1.61, I = 39%, n = 2). These findings provide evidence for a positive association between both general and abdominal adiposity and the risk of aortic dissection, with the strongest associations observed for high waist-to-height ratio. Although further large-scale studies are warranted for confirmation, these findings suggest avoiding excess weight may be an important strategy for the prevention of aortic dissection.

title: Long-term outcome of stenting for the iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral arterio-venous graft; a case series.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the possible etiology and evaluate the technical and clinical outcomes of using bare metal stents for the treatment of central venous stenosis (CVS) in the lower extremity with ipsilateral hemodialysis access. METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis of a small case series was conducted in hemodialysis patients with lower extremity arteriovenous grafts (AVG) who were treated with bare metal stents (BMS) for symptomatic iliac vein stenosis between April 2016 and June 2021. Patients' demographic data, technical details, adverse events, clinical outcomes, and imaging data were recorded. RESULTS: The study cohort comprised seven females and four males, with a mean age of 58.8 ± 13.4 years. Preoperative lower limb venography was performed in nine patients scheduled for AVG creation. With the exception of one case demonstrating left iliac vein compression, the iliac veins were patent in all other patients. Symptoms of lower limb swelling developed at a mean interval of 9.40 ± 5.83 months (range: 3-20 months) following AVG placement. Eight cases had a concomitant history of temporary ipsilateral femoral vein catheterization. Lesion characteristics included nine stenotic lesions and two occlusive lesions. All patients were treated with SMART Control stents (Cordis Corp, USA). The technical success rate was 100%, and symptomatic relief was achieved in all cases. Over a mean follow-up period of 47.8 ± 31.7 months (range: 10-123 months), the target lesion primary patency was 100% (one-side confidence interval [CI] = 0.74,1). CONCLUSIONS: Using BMS is a safe and effective method to treat iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral AVG.

title: Bilateral peripheral CT venography for evaluating central venous lesions in dysfunctional arteriovenous fistulas: feasibility, safety, and radiation dose in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Central venous stenosis and occlusion are major causes of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) dysfunction in hemodialysis patients. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, radiation exposure, and anatomical findings of bilateral peripheral CT venography for central venous assessment in patients with dysfunctional AVFs. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 46 consecutive hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs who underwent bilateral peripheral CT venography between August 2023 and June 2025. Technical success, procedure-related adverse events, radiation dose parameters, central venous lesion characteristics, and agreement with available comparative imaging modalities were analyzed. Comparative imaging findings from puncture-based angiography and/or duplex ultrasonography were assessed descriptively. RESULTS: All 46 examinations were technically successful (100%), with a mean procedure duration of 4 minutes (range, 3-5 minutes). Minor adverse events included one patient of contrast extravasation (2.2%) and 3 of mild allergic reactions (6.5%); no severe procedure-related complications were documented. The mean CTDIvol and DLP were 11.87 mGy and 784.15 mGy·cm, respectively. Central venous abnormalities were identified in 44 patients (95.7%), including stenosis in 31 (67.4%), occlusion in 11 (23.9%), and aneurysmal changes in 2 (4.3%). Comparative imaging was available in 38 patients, and CT venography showed agreement with available findings in 37 cases (97.4%). This agreement was interpreted as descriptive concordance rather than formal diagnostic accuracy. CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral peripheral CT venography demonstrated high technical feasibility, acceptable safety, and effective visualization of central venous abnormalities in hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs. Further prospective studies are needed to validate its diagnostic performance and clinical impact. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This technique enables efficient, noninvasive assessment of central venous pathology with minimal risk, supporting its potential as a practical alternative to conventional imaging in hemodialysis patients.

title: Transarterial Computed Tomographic Angiography in Patients With Impaired Renal Function Undergoing Endovascular Aortic Repair.
abstract: P PurposeComputed tomography angiography (CTA) is crucial for preoperative planning and postoperative surveillance of endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). Renal function impairment however limits pre- and postoperative assessment. The aim of our study was to evaluate the safety and diagnostic value of a novel technique in the setting of patients undergoing EVAR.Methods216 patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing transbrachial placement of an angiography catheter in the aorta for contrast medium administration were analyzed retrospectively. 45 patients with normal kidney function and aortic aneurysms were included as control group. 27 were female, 84 cases were for thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm, while 106 cases were for abdominal aortic aneurysm. Primary endpoint was the freedom from contrast-induced acute kidney injury. Secondary safety endpoints were freedom from access site complications and cerebrovascular incidents. Imaging quality endpoints were attenuation values and contrast-to-noise-ratios in predefined vessels, validated by intraclass correlation coefficients.ResultsMean creatinine change was -.11 mg/dL, mean GFR change was 2.13% in the intervention group. There were 10 (4.6%) false aneurysms and two access site hematoma (0.93%). Two cerebrovascular incidents (0.9%) were transient. Transarterial CTA attenuation values varied between 210.4 (±89) and 241.4 (±98) Hounsfield units (HU), and 306.35 (±63.27) to 321.39 (±70.12) HU in the control group. The mean amount of contrast medium used in the catheter group was significantly reduced (31.70 ± 5.82 mL) compared to the control group (= .001). Contrast-to-noise ratios varied between 9.1 (±4.6) and 11.1 (±4.4. Intraclass correlation coefficients between the readings were very good (0.987-0.992).ConclusionCatheter-based transarterial computed tomographic angiography is a safe and efficacious way to evaluate patients with aortic aneurysms, both prior and after EVAR.

title: Perioperative management of acute type A aortic dissection using extended half-life factor IX (Alprolix) in a patient with severe hemophilia B: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Emergency surgery for acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) in patients with severe hemophilia B is extremely rare, and perioperative coagulation management is a major challenge. CASE PRESENTATION: A 63-year-old man with severe hemophilia B (factor IX activity < 1%) was diagnosed with ATAAD and underwent emergency surgery. Replacement therapy with an extended half-life factor IX product (eftrenonacog alfa; Alprolix) was administered targeting a factor IX activity of 80-100%, and total arch replacement was performed. Cardiopulmonary bypass was performed under standard heparinization conditions. Since rapid measurement of factor IX activity was not possible, postoperative replacement therapy was based primarily on the clinical assessment of hemostasis, with serial activated partial thromboplastin time measurements providing supportive information, whereas intraoperative anticoagulation was managed using standard activated clotting time monitoring. Intra- and postoperative bleeding volumes were within ranges comparable to those observed in standard complex aortic surgery, and the postoperative course was uneventful. CONCLUSIONS: The use of an extended half-life factor IX product may be a practical option for perioperative coagulation management during emergency aortic surgery in patients with severe hemophilia B.

title: Integrative genetic analyses for drug repurposing identify emodin as a candidate modulator of STAT3 signaling in abdominal aortic aneurysm.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening vascular disease lacking effective pharmacological therapies. To identify potential therapeutic targets and candidate compounds, we performed integrative genetic analyses for drug repurposing by combining Mendelian randomization (MR), summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), and Bayesian colocalization. This framework prioritized multiple druggable candidates, among which STAT3 emerged as a key regulatory node. Subsequent functional studies demonstrated that emodin suppressed vascular smooth muscle cell proliferation, migration, phenotypic switching, and inflammatory responses. These effects were accompanied by reduced STAT3 phosphorylation and nuclear localization. Molecular docking suggested a potential binding mode of emodin within the STAT3 SH2 domain, while cellular thermal shift assays demonstrated thermal stabilization of STAT3 by emodin in intact cells, consistent with target engagement. Notably, emodin and the selective STAT3 inhibitor STAT3-IN-13 produced comparable effects, and co-treatment did not yield additive efficacy, suggesting overlapping mechanisms. In vivo, emodin attenuated aneurysm development and reduced vascular inflammation in experimental models. Collectively, these findings identify emodin as a candidate modulator of AAA progression acting through suppression of STAT3-associated signaling pathways, and demonstrate the potential of genetic evidence-guided drug repurposing strategies in complex vascular diseases.

title: Early and follow-up results of reinterventions for type 2 endoleak following endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm (EVAR): the multicenter REinterventions for Type 2 Endoleak (RETE) study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type II endoleak (T2EL) is frequent after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) and may require reintervention in selected patients. However, the optimal treatment strategy for durable resolution remains uncertain. The aim of this study is to retrospectively analyze perioperative and long-term results of T2Els' reinterventions, both endovascular and open surgical, in a large patient cohort from twenty high-volume academic centers. METHODS: A retrospective analysis of consecutive patients undergoing first reintervention for T2ELs was conducted across 20 centers over a 10-year period. Patients requiring concomitant treatment for other endoleak types were excluded. A total of 403 patients were included. Primary outcomes included technical success, 30-day AAA-related mortality and reintervention-free survival during follow-up. Secondary outcomes were perioperative complications, early reintervention, overall survival, freedom from aneurysm-related death and rupture, freedom from recurrent endoleaks, freedom from open conversion or semi-conversion in patients previously treated endovascularly and sac behavior during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression analyses were performed to analyze follow-up results. RESULTS: Patients were predominantly male (90%) with a mean age of 77 years. Reintervention was indicated for sac enlargement in 94.5% of cases; 4% presented with rupture. Median time from EVAR to reintervention was 4.3 years. Lumbar arteries (55%) and the inferior mesenteric artery (35%) were the main sources. Endovascular treatment was performed in 86% and open conversion/semi-conversion in 14%. Technical success was 96%, with 1% mortality and 4% major complications. Overall survival was 80.5% and rupture-free survival 79.2% at 5 years. Recurrent T2EL occurred in 64.2%, and reintervention-free survival was 48.3%. Endovascular group showed significantly lower freedom from reintervention rates when compared to open conversion/semi conversion group (42.4% vs 86.8%, SE 0.04 vs SE 0.05, p<0.001, log-rank 15.9). Conversion/semi-conversion after endovascular treatment occurred in 14%. No differences were recorded comparing different fabric materials of the endograft in terms of freedom for reintervention and freedom from open surgery. A sac diameter ≥7 cm at the time of reintervention predicted further reinterventions, while primary open treatment improved durability. CONCLUSIONS: Reinterventions for T2ELs are safe, with satisfactory immediate technical success and low perioperative mortality. During follow-up, risks of rupture and AAA-related death remain low. However, the endoleak recurrence rate exceeds 60% at five years, necessitating reintervention in over 40% of patients. Early intervention for patients with a sac diameter approaching 7 cm can be suggested, while a primary open approach may be considered in low-risk patients.

The aim of this study is to retrospectively analyze perioperative and long-term results of T2Els' reinterventions, both endovascular and open surgical, in a large patient cohort from twenty high-volume academic centers.

title: Risk Factors and Clinical Outcomes of Reocclusion after Endovascular Treatment for Acute Ischemic Stroke: An Updated Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Early reocclusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is underrecognized; its determinants and impact remain poorly defined. METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE. Post hoc sensitivity analyses included only same-site reocclusion definitions. RESULTS: Ten studies (3,381 patients) were included; 244 (7.2%) reoccluded. Reocclusion was associated with lower 90-day functional independence (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.17-0.38) and higher mortality (OR 1.86, 1.29-2.68), both moderate certainty. Reocclusion was more frequent with large-artery atherosclerosis (OR 2.24, 1.41-3.55; same-site 3.04, 1.73-5.33) and less frequent with cardioembolism (OR 0.40, 0.28-0.57) and atrial fibrillation (OR 0.39, 0.26-0.59), mutually confounded associations reflecting one embolic-versus-atherothrombotic axis. Prestroke antiplatelet therapy (OR 0.43, 0.28-0.67) lost significance under the same-site definition (0.60, 0.31-1.16). Exploratory data (two cohorts) linked eTICI 2c-3 reperfusion with less reocclusion (OR 0.44, 0.28-0.69). No study reported when etiology was adjudicated; the atherosclerosis association may be partly outcome-induced. CONCLUSIONS: Early reocclusion is uncommon but carries a substantial prognostic penalty. Its determinants appear to lie in the vascular substrate rather than thrombectomy technique; prospective studies with uniform same-site definitions and systematic follow-up imaging are needed.

title: Effect of Extended-Duration Venous Thromboprophylaxis After Cancer Surgery.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cancer patients undergoing surgery are at significantly increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). Although extended thromboprophylaxis is recommended, the optimal anticoagulant type and duration remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of different extended thromboprophylaxis in this population. METHODS: A Bayesian network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was performed to evaluate various thromboprophylaxis strategies for patients undergoing cancer-related surgery. We conducted both three-node and five-node network analyses to evaluate extended-duration versus standard-duration thromboprophylaxis strategies. Outcomes included venous thromboembolism, major bleeding, and all-cause mortality. Net clinical benefit and risk-benefit assessments were additionally performed to determine the overall impact of prolonged anticoagulant therapy. Treatment effects were summarized as risk ratios (RRs) with corresponding 95% credible intervals (CrIs). RESULTS: A total of 14 randomized controlled trials involving 4,331 participants were included. Compared with placebo, extended-duration prophylaxis with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) (RR 0.12, 95% CrI 0.05-0.27) and low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) (RR 0.17, 95% CrI 0.05-0.55) significantly reduced the incidence of venous thromboembolism without a corresponding increase in major bleeding. In net clinical benefit analyses, both prolonged DOAC therapy (RR 0.27, 95% CrI 0.14-0.49) and LMWH (RR 0.36, 95% CrI 0.17-0.76) demonstrated favorable overall outcomes. Risk-benefit evaluation suggested that prolonged DOACs provided a more advantageous balance than LMWH, with an NNH/NNT ratio of 4.17. CONCLUSIONS: Extended thromboprophylaxis is effective and safe for cancer patients undergoing surgery. Besides, DOACs appears to be the optimal anticoagulant for extended thromboprophylaxis, providing the greatest net clinical benefit.

title: Characterizing the Thrombotic Spectrum and Clinical Phenotypes of Tranexamic Acid-Associated Adverse Events: A Pharmacovigilance Study Based on the FAERS Database.
abstract: Tranexamic acid (TXA) is widely used to reduce bleeding in surgical, trauma, obstetric, and gynecological settings. However, concerns remain regarding TXA-associated thrombotic adverse events, and their phenotypic heterogeneity and clinical severity have not been comprehensively characterized. This study investigated TXA-associated thrombotic events using the Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) from 2004Q1 to 2026Q1. Thrombotic adverse events were identified using the Standardized MedDRA Query (SMQ) "Embolic and thrombotic events" and evaluated by disproportionality analysis based on reporting odds ratios (RORs). Qualifying thrombotic events were assigned to the SMQ vessel-type subgroups-arterial, vessel-type unspecified/mixed, and venous-and demographic characteristics, indications, clinical outcomes and time-to-onset were compared across subgroups; signal strength was further related to clinical severity. In all, 515 thrombotic cases associated with TXA and 26 selected thrombotic terms were found (arterial, 157; mixed, 168; venous, 190). Venous thromboembolism-pulmonary embolism (n = 128, ROR 13.94) and deep vein thrombosis (n = 58, ROR 9.09)-is the most frequent type and brings about the most severe and fatal consequences (death reported in 16.8% of venous versus 2.5% of arterial reports), whereas the strongest disproportionality signals were observed for rare site-specific events such as ovarian vein thrombosis (ROR 352.95) and cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (ROR 118.35). The three subgroups differed markedly in demographic and clinical characteristics: venous events occurred predominantly in women (73.7%) treated for menorrhagia (35.3%), whereas arterial events arose mainly in surgical or procedural settings (intravenous route 36.3%; surgery/prophylaxis 19.1%) and presented earliest after exposure [median time-to-onset (TTO) 0 versus 7 days]. Signal strength was not concordant with clinical severity across the thrombotic spectrum. These findings provide a deeper understanding of the thrombotic safety of TXA, indicate that the clinical background may influence the phenotypic differences among the different thrombotic types, and emphasize the necessity of enhanced attention and risk stratification in high-risk groups.

title: Percutaneous and Endovascular Embolization-Based Treatments of Type 1A and Type 1B Endoleaks after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair.
abstract: ObjectiveThis retrospective, observational study was conducted to evaluate the efficacy of embolization-based treatments for Types 1A and 1B endoleaks following endovascular aneurysm repair.DesignA total of 26 patients who underwent endovascular aneurysm repair between January 2005 and September 2023 and subsequently received embolization therapy for Types 1A or 1B endoleak, either at the end of the procedure or during follow-up, were retrospectively reviewed.MethodsEmbolization was performed in 16 patients with Type 1A endoleaks and 10 with Type 1B. Eight of the 16 patients who underwent embolization for Type 1A endoleaks required additional treatments such as aortic cuff placement or a chimney graft. Similarly, six out of the 10 patients treated with embolization for Type 1B endoleaks underwent adjunctive procedures such as iliac stent-graft extension. The primary endpoint was the absence of aneurysm sac enlargement. Secondary endpoints included technical success and the avoidance of endoleak-related reintervention.ResultsAneurysm sac regression or stabilization was observed in 68.7% of Type 1A and 70% of Type 1B endoleak cases over mean follow-up periods of 43.1 and 22.3 months, respectively.ConclusionEmbolization-based endovascular treatment, alone or combined with adjunctive endograft procedures, may achieve aneurysm sac stabilization or regression in a substantial proportion of patients with Types 1A and 1B endoleaks. However, the possibility of recurrence and reintervention, particularly in Type 1A endoleaks, remains an important limitation of this approach and warrants continued imaging surveillance.

title: Use of vaginal estrogens in urogynecology: current evidence, controversies and clinical applications.
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is a prevalent yet underrecognized condition in postmenopausal women, characterized by progressive vulvovaginal and lower urinary tract symptoms from estrogen deficiency. Vaginal estrogen therapy is the first-line pharmacologic treatment for GSM. However, as new evidence emerges, understanding of its efficacy, safety, and use in special populations continues to evolve. This review summarizes current evidence on vaginal estrogen formulations, clinical effectiveness, safety, and therapeutic applications. RECENT FINDINGS: Recent randomized controlled trials confirm that low-dose vaginal estrogen significantly improves GSM symptoms - including vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, and irritation - while restoring epithelial integrity and normalizing pH. Evidence also supports its role in reducing recurrent urinary tract infections by restoring lactobacilli-dominant flora, reinforced by a 2025 multisociety clinical guideline recommending topical, but not systemic, estrogen for this indication. Comparative studies show similar efficacy across creams, tablets, inserts, and rings, differing primarily in convenience and absorption rather than effectiveness. Large cohort studies indicate no increased risk of cardiovascular disease, venous thromboembolism, or malignancy. Use in breast cancer survivors remains controversial, but emerging data suggest minimal systemic absorption and no clear increase in recurrence risk, supporting shared decision-making. In addition, long-term outcomes show that adjunctive vaginal estrogen does not improve anatomic surgical success after native tissue apical prolapse repair. Nonhormonal therapies and agents like ospemifene or prasterone offer alternative options, though they demonstrate lower or more variable efficacy than vaginal estrogen. SUMMARY: Vaginal estrogen therapy is the most effective, evidence-based treatment for GSM and helps prevent recurrent urinary tract infections in postmenopausal women. Its favorable safety profile and multiple formulations enable individualized care. Recent evidence clarifies that while overall safety is reassuring, caution is necessary for breast cancer survivors using aromatase inhibitors. Additionally, longer-term perioperative trial data temper expectations regarding surgical-recurrence benefits, while confirming its value for local tissue optimization. Ongoing research should focus on long-term safety in high-risk groups and the effectiveness of emerging non-estrogen alternatives.

title: Ultrasound-Guided versus Fluoroscopy-Guided Femoral Access for Structural Heart Procedures: Outcomes From Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation and Left Atrial Appendage Closure.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Transfemoral access is the default approach for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and left atrial appendage closure (LAAC). Although ultrasound (US)-guided femoral puncture improves first-pass success and reduces vascular complications in randomized trials, real-world data in contemporary structural heart interventions, including both arterial and venous large-sheath access, remain limited. The authors aimed to compare US-guided vs. conventional transfemoral access in patients undergoing TAVI and LAAC. METHODS: This single-center, retrospective cohort study included 165 consecutive patients undergoing transfemoral structural procedures between January 2022 and December 2024 (93: TAVI; 72: LAAC). Ultrasound guidance was used in 57 procedures (34.5%). Arterial and venous cohorts were analyzed separately. Primary outcomes were absolute hemoglobin decrease (ΔHb) and access-site vascular complications (hematoma, pseudoaneurysm, and arteriovenous fistula). In the arterial cohort, 1 : 1 propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline differences. RESULTS: Hemoglobin decline was significantly smaller with US guidance in both venous (0.80 ± 0.95 vs. 1.50 ± 1.11 g/dL; P = .009) and arterial procedures (0.58 ± 0.97 vs. 1.29 ± 1.00 g/dL; P = .002). In the venous cohort, complication rates were numerically lower but not statistically different (3.8% vs. 17.4%; P = .143). In contrast, arterial complications were significantly reduced with US guidance. After propensity matching (31 patients per group), complications occurred in 3.2% vs. 29.0% [Absolute Risk Reduction(ARR) = 25.8%, Number Need to Treat (NNT) = 4, P = .013]. CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided transfemoral access was associated with reduced hemoglobin decline and fewer vascular complications, particularly in large-bore arterial procedures, supporting routine integration of real-time US guidance in structural interventions.

title: Access Vessel Patency After Endovascular Therapy via Tibiopedal Access in Patients With Lower Extremity Artery Disease.
abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the access vessel patency after endovascular therapy performed via tibiopedal access. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a retrospective, single-center, observational study. Patients who underwent endovascular therapy via tibiopedal access with sheath insertion were enrolled. The primary outcome was loss of access vessel patency defined as access vessel occlusion or stenosis with a peak systolic velocity ratio > 2.4 on duplex ultrasound at 6 months. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify the predictors of access vessel patency loss, with hemodialysis, severely calcified access vessel and sheath-to-artery ratio included as covariates. RESULTS: A total of 95 limbs in 91 patients were included in this study, and loss of access vessel patency was observed in 22 limbs (23.1%). Multivariate logistic regression analysis demonstrated that sheath-to-artery ratio was the only independent predictor (odds ratio: 1.493, 95% confidence interval: 1.130-1.976; p = 0.005). The receiver operating characteristic curve analysis revealed that the optimal cutoff value of sheath-to-artery ratio for predicting loss of access vessel patency was 1.08, with an area under the curve of 0.723. In this cohort, the 2-year freedom from major adverse limb events were 98.6% (95% CI: 90.8-99.8%), and no major amputation occurred. CONCLUSION: The present study demonstrated a relatively high incidence of loss of access vessel patency after endovascular therapy via tibiopedal access, although this was not associated with an increase in major adverse limb events. A larger sheath-to-artery ratio was identified as an independent predictor of loss of access vessel patency.

title: Endovascular Salvage of Dysfunctional Native Haemodialysis Arteriovenous Fistulas: Clinical Outcomes and Predictors of Patency.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypofunctioning haemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas are an important cause of inadequate dialysis, access failure and morbidity in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), and timely catheter-based intervention may help restore access function and prolong fistula usability. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy, feasibility, and safety of catheter-based interventional procedures for hypofunctioning haemodialysis fistulas in patients with CKD. METHODS: This single-centre, retrospective observational follow up study, enrolled with 100 CKD patients on maintenance haemodialysis with dysfunctional native arteriovenous fistulas who underwent fistulogram and catheter-based intervention. RESULTS: The mean age was 57.2 ± 12.4 years, 62.0% were male, and hypertension (80.0%) and diabetes mellitus (57.0%) were the major comorbidities. Radio cephalic fistula was the commonest access type (46.0%), and inadequate dialysis was the leading presentation (73.0%). Fistulography showed significant stenosis in 96.0%, with central vein involvement in 43.0% and long-segment lesions in 56.0%. Angioplasty was attempted in 96.0%, achieving technical success in 91.7% of attempted interventions and clinical success in 85.0%. Stenosis and pressure gradient reduced significantly after intervention (both p<0.001). Complications occurred in 13.0%, with no deaths. Primary patency declined from 82.0% at 1 month to 58.0% at 6 months and 38.0% at 12 months. Patency loss was independently predicted by older age, central vein lesions, long lesions, residual stenosis, and absent post-procedure thrill. CONCLUSION: Catheter-based endovascular intervention may be an effective fistula-salvage strategy for hypofunctioning haemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas, although long-term patency was influenced by lesion complexity, residual stenosis and restoration of post-procedure thrill.

title: Percutaneous approach to aortic disease: EVAR, TEVAR and newer techniques for more proximal disease.
abstract: Advances in device design, imaging and vascular-closure technology have driven a progressive shift from surgical femoral exposure to totally percutaneous strategies for endovascular aortic repair. This narrative review summarises contemporary evidence and practical considerations for percutaneous access across the spectrum of aortic disease, from infrarenal endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) to thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR), fenestrated/branched repair and endovascular treatment of the aortic arch. Percutaneous femoral access is now supported by randomized evidence, large registries and administrative cohorts showing high technical success, fewer wound complications, shorter operative times and shorter hospital stay compared with routine surgical cutdown, and real-time ultrasound-guided puncture has become a guideline-endorsed standard of care. Major contemporary developments include computed tomography-based access planning centred on calcification burden and sheath-to-artery ratio; an individualised, anatomy-driven choice between suture- and plug-based closure devices; endovascular preparation of hostile iliofemoral anatomy with pave-and-crack, endoconduits and intravascular lithotripsy; low-profile endografts that have widened transfemoral eligibility; and percutaneous axillary and carotid routes that enable complex TEVAR, fenestrated/branched and selected arch repairs in experienced centres, although evidence for these latter applications remains largely observational. Looking ahead, further reductions in delivery-system profile, dedicated large-bore closure technologies, image-fusion guidance and off-the-shelf branched devices are expected to extend fully percutaneous repair to increasingly complex anatomy, while prospective, aortic-specific and device-level comparisons with standardized anatomical metrics and long-term follow-up are needed to refine patient selection and confirm durable limb and target-vessel patency.

title: Heterogeneity in Time-Outcome Associations After Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Binational Registry Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although "time is brain" remains a core principle in acute stroke care, the association between treatment timing and functional outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) varies across patients. Some individuals treated in extended time windows still achieve favorable outcomes, a phenomenon termed the "late window paradox." Differences in stroke pathophysiology across etiologies may contribute to heterogeneity in the time-outcome relationship after EVT. We investigated factors associated with heterogeneity in time-dependent EVT responsiveness, with particular attention to stroke etiology. METHODS: We analyzed data from two multicenter registries in Korea (CRCS-K) and Taiwan (TREAT-AIS) from January 2019 to April 2023. Patients with anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism (CE) or large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) were included. Multivariable regression and interaction analyses were performed to evaluate the association between onset-to-puncture (OTP) time and 90-day functional outcomes and to identify effect modifiers. RESULTS: _interaction Among 4,719 patients (mean age 72.0 years; 42.9% women; median NIHSS 15), longer OTP time was associated with lower odds of 90-day functional independence (adjusted OR per hour, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.98; p=0.001). The impact of OTP time varied by stroke characteristics. CE etiology, MCA occlusion, higher NIHSS, and male sex were associated with greater time sensitivity. In CE strokes, each hour of delay reduced the odds of functional independence by 4% (aOR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.94-0.97; p<0.001), whereas no significant association was observed in LAA strokes (P=0.028). CONCLUSION: The association between EVT timing and functional outcome varies according to stroke etiology and clinical characteristics, highlighting heterogeneity in time-outcome relationships among EVT-treated patients and providing observational insight into outcome variability in extended treatment windows.

Differences in stroke pathophysiology across etiologies may contribute to heterogeneity in the time-outcome relationship after EVT. We investigated factors associated with heterogeneity in time-dependent EVT responsiveness, with particular attention to stroke etiology.

title: A pilot study of the InVera Infusion Device: Twelve-month outcomes in the treatment of incompetent saphenous veins.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The InVera Infusion Device is a novel catheter designed for the delivery of sclerosant agents during non-thermal, non-tumescent (NTNT) ablation of incompetent superficial truncal veins of the lower extremity. This device pilot study aimed to evaluate the technical success, safety, and 12-month clinical outcome. METHODS: A single-center, prospective pilot study enrolled 10 patients with primary symptomatic axial reflux who underwent chemical ablation procedures with sclerosant delivery using the InVera Infusion Device. Primary outcomes assessed were technical procedural success, adverse events, Revised Venous Clinical Severity Score (rVCSS), patient-reported outcomes (PROs) based on a HASTI (Heaviness, Achiness, Swelling, Throbbing, Itching) symptom questionnaire and anatomical success rates from duplex ultrasound examination at baseline, 1 week, 8 weeks, 3, 6, and 12 months post procedure. Baseline and 12 months post procedure were compared for both the rVCSS and the HASTI results using a paired t-test and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test respectively RESULTS: Technical procedural success was 100%. There were no device-related adverse events or serious adverse events including no deep vein thrombosis recorded throughout the follow-up period. Clinician assessed rVCSS and patient reported HASTI scores both showed statistically significant reductions from baseline to 12 months (adjusted p = 0.03 for both). Ultrasound-based anatomical assessment at 12 months demonstrated elimination of abnormal reflux and complete or partial occlusion in 90% of patients. CONCLUSIONS: The InVera Infusion device provides a safe and effective technique for the delivery of sclerosant agents as part of the management of incompetent saphenous veins, demonstrating favorable 12-month anatomical, clinical and patient reported outcomes in this pilot cohort.

title: Systematic Review of Devices, Designs, and Trials for the Treatment of Deep Venous Reflux.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) is driven primarily by venous reflux and affects nearly one-third of adults. While superficial reflux is effectively treated with ablation, therapeutic options for deep venous reflux (DVR) remain limited. Despite decades of innovation, no prosthetic or bioprosthetic venous valve has achieved U.S. regulatory approval. We systematically reviewed device strategies, clinical and hemodynamic outcomes, complications, and barriers to translation for devices designed to treat DVR. METHODS: We conducted a PROSPERO-registered systematic review (CRD420251101761) of six databases from inception through February 2026, including in vivo animal and human studies evaluating prosthetic or bioprosthetic devices for DVR. Studies of native valve repair or autotransplantation were excluded. The primary outcome for human studies was clinical improvement, and secondary outcomes included patency, procedural complications, valvular function, and thrombosis. RESULTS: Of 516 records identified, 15 met inclusion criteria: 8 human and 7 animal studies. Two principal strategies were identified: intraluminal valve restoration (VR) and external compression (EC), with approximately 40% of devices delivered percutaneously or endovenously. In human studies, technical success ranged from 87.7%-100%, patency from 67%-100%, and perioperative complication rates from 0%-44%, consisting primarily of bleeding, wound infection, and valve thrombosis. Valve occlusion occurred in up to 28% of animal implants and 18%-22% of select human cohorts. Two perioperative deaths occurred in animal studies; none were reported in human studies. Among human studies, valve competency assessment methods varied substantially. Reported competency ranged from 0%-92%, reflecting heterogeneity in imaging modalities and definitions. Discordance between anatomic patency, duplex-derived reflux reduction, and clinical improvement was frequently observed. In contemporary multicenter trial data, fewer than half of patients met predefined reflux-reduction endpoints despite high device patency and substantial clinical improvement, highlighting discordance between anatomic, hemodynamic, and patient-centered outcomes. By one year, pain had improved in 75%-97% of patients; rVCSS decreased by 37%-81%, with clinically meaningful (≥3-point) improvement in up to 84.6%; and ulcer healing ranged from 67%-100%. Longer follow-up extended to 2 years in animal studies and up to 11 years in human series with various outcomes reported. CONCLUSION: Several devices developed for DVR have demonstrated technical feasibility and symptom improvement. However, the risk of thrombosis, the marginal impact on valvular function, and the lack of standardization and selection of adequate endpoints in the measurement of results remain major barriers to regulatory approval. Standardized composite endpoints integrating objective hemodynamic measures with patient-centered outcomes are essential to advance durable DVR device development and clinical translation.

title: Admission C-Reactive Protein-to-Albumin Ratio Is Associated With Early Major Amputation After Minor Amputation in Patients With Infected Foot Wounds.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Minor amputation is commonly performed as a limb-salvage procedure for infected foot wounds; however, some patients experience early limb-salvage failure and progress to major amputation. Reliable biomarkers predicting early failure remain limited. PURPOSE: To evaluate whether the admission C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) is associated with major amputation within 90 days after minor amputation in patients with infected foot wounds. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study. METHODS: Patients who underwent minor amputation for infected foot wounds between March 2005 and September 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. Of 358 screened patients, 257 met the inclusion criteria. Admission CAR was calculated from C-reactive protein and serum albumin levels. The primary outcome was major amputation within 90 days. Univariable logistic regression and multivariable Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed. Predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. RESULTS: Among 257 patients, 60 (23.3%) progressed to major amputation within 90 days. Higher admission CAR values were significantly associated with major amputation. CAR remained an independent predictor in multivariable analysis (hazard ratio 1.17; 95% confidence interval 1.05-1.31; p value = .004). Adding CAR improved the predictive performance of the baseline model (area under the curve .883 vs .810). CONCLUSIONS: Admission CAR is a simple and independent factor associated with early major amputation after minor amputation and may help facilitate early risk stratification. LEVEL OF CLINICAL EVIDENCE: Level III.

title: Collapse and Thrombosis of an Iliac Branch Endovascular Device Following Blunt Force Trauma.
abstract: Iliac branch endovascular device thrombosis following blunt force trauma has rarely been reported. We describe an 81-year-old man who developed proximal aortobiiliac endograft collapse with subsequent thrombosis after blunt force trauma occurring two months following endovascular aneurysm repair. The patient delayed vascular follow-up for one year and later presented at routine surveillance with progressive bilateral hip and buttock claudication. Despite chronic therapeutic anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation, the patient developed progressive thrombosis with ischemic symptoms. The case highlights a rare mechanical cause of post-EVAR aortoiliac thrombosis and demonstrates the importance of early vascular imaging and consultation following traumatic injury in post-EVAR patients.

title: Volumetric Analysis versus Diameter Measurement for Early Detection of Post-EVAR Sac Progression.
abstract: 2 P ObjectiveTo compare diameter- and volume-based surveillance after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and determine whether volumetric sac assessment identifies postoperative remodeling not captured by conventional maximum diameter measurement.MethodsThis retrospective single-center study included 383 patients who underwent elective EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm between January 2016 and April 2024. All patients had preoperative and postoperative computed tomography angiography and at least 1 year of follow-up. Maximum sac diameter, total aneurysm sac volume, thrombus volume, thrombus density, neck morphology, and other anatomical variables were assessed using standardized morphometric and three-dimensional morphovolumetric measurements. Sac dynamics were classified by diameter criteria (≥5 mm decrease, stable, or ≥5 mm increase) and volumetric criteria (>10% decrease, stable, or >10% increase).ResultsEndoleaks occurred in 26.1% of patients (n = 100), and secondary interventions were required in 14.1% (n = 54), with a mean time to reintervention of 21.7 ± 10 months. At final follow-up, 74.7% demonstrated sac diameter reduction, 18.5% were stable, and 6.8% had enlargement, whereas volumetric analysis showed shrinkage in 81.7%, stability in 6.0%, and enlargement in 12.3%. At 1, 6, and 12 months, cohort mean diameter changed by -0.6%, -3.1%, and -6.5% from baseline, respectively, while cohort mean volume changed by -0.5%, -5.7%, and -12.5%. Among diameter-stable sacs, 32.4% enlarged volumetrically and 38.0% regressed volumetrically. In enlarging sacs, a 10% volume increase corresponded to an approximately 4 mm diameter increase (R= 0.72;< 0.001); this 4 mm value was a regression estimate, not the diameter threshold used for sac classification. Preoperative morphometric and morphovolumetric variables were associated with endoleak and secondary intervention in exploratory analyses.ConclusionVolumetric sac analysis identified additional postoperative remodeling beyond maximum diameter measurement, particularly in apparently stable sacs. A practical surveillance strategy combining rapid diameter-based screening with selective volumetric analysis in stable, borderline, or clinically suspicious cases may improve recognition of adverse sac behavior without requiring routine volumetry in every follow-up study.

title: Initial Direct Oral Anticoagulants Versus Warfarin After Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Target Trial Emulation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vitamin K antagonists have traditionally been used after cerebral venous thrombosis, whereas direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly prescribed. Whether DOACs are noninferior to warfarin for preventing 1-year symptomatic recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain. METHODS: We conducted a registry-based target trial emulation in a bidirectional multicenter Chinese cerebral venous thrombosis registry (retrospective phase, 2015-2022; prospective phase, 2023-2025). Eligible patients were adults with imaging-confirmed cerebral venous thrombosis who initiated either a DOAC or warfarin within 30 days after diagnosis. Time zero was the date of the first oral anticoagulant prescription. The primary efficacy outcome was symptomatic recurrent VTE within 1 year. Propensity score overlap weighting was used, and weighted Fine-Gray models treated death as a competing event. The clinically acceptable noninferiority margin was defined as an absolute increase of 1.5 percentage points in 1-year recurrent VTE risk, corresponding approximately to a relative margin of 1.50 for the primary Fine-Gray analysis. RESULTS: P P Among 2476 eligible patients, 942 initiated a DOAC (rivaroxaban, n=701; dabigatran, n=121; apixaban, n=113; edoxaban, n=7) and 1534 initiated warfarin. Within 1 year, symptomatic recurrent VTE occurred in 36 and 73 patients, respectively. The overlap-weighted 1-year recurrence risks were 3.74% and 5.47%, corresponding to a risk difference of -1.73 percentage points (95% CI, -3.76 to 0.30). DOAC treatment was associated with a lower subdistribution hazard ratio of 0.67 compared with that of warfarin ([95% CI, 0.37-1.21];=0.184), meeting the prespecified noninferiority criterion (for noninferiority=0.004). Major bleeding was rare within 1 year (0 versus 1 patient). Clinical nonmajor bleeding occurred in 18 versus 34 patients, and any bleeding occurred in 48 versus 75 patients. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with cerebral venous thrombosis selected for oral anticoagulation, initial treatment with a DOAC met the noninferiority criterion relative to warfarin for the prevention of symptomatic recurrent VTE at 1 year. Findings regarding bleeding outcomes were exploratory and do not permit conclusions regarding comparative safety or equivalence.

title: Predictors of Surveillance Imaging Non-compliance Among Patients with TEVAR for Blunt Thoracic Aortic Injury.
abstract: P P ObjectivesBlunt Thoracic Aortic Injury (BTAI) is the second leading cause of death for patients with blunt trauma. Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) has become the standard of care for high-grade BTAI, reducing morbidity and mortality while requiring long-term surveillance imaging to ensure graft integrity and prevent future complications. However, adherence to this protocol is poor. Previous studies evaluating the factors associated with post-operative imaging non-compliance have yielded conflicting results. This study aimed to evaluate predictors of post-TEVAR non-compliance inpatients presenting with BTAI.MethodsA retrospective study on 23 patients was conducted using a single institution Aortic Center Database (2015-2025). Inclusion criteria included patients who were age >18 years and underwent TEVAR for BTAI. Demographic, comorbidity, hospital course, and follow-up data were collected. The Distressed Communities Index (DCI) score was derived from patient's home address ZIP code. Time-to-event analysis defined loss to follow up (LTFU) for vascular imaging as the failure event. Patients were censored at death or if compliant through 1 year following the index TEVAR. Statistical analysis included chi-square, t-tests, and Kaplan-Meier survival.ResultsBased on this single-center review on TEVAR follow-up for BTAI, sex, race, and hospital length of stay did not impact compliance. Medical comorbidities were also non-significant. Patients who presented with a lower injury severity score (= 0.02) and lived more than 20 miles from their follow-up appointment (= 0.02) were more likely to be LTFU. While the type of facility was not impactful, all patients who were discharged to a non-home location were LTFU. Interestingly, DCI and insurance status had no impact on follow-up non-compliance.ConclusionsThis study supports the development of targeted, patient-centered surveillance strategies, especially amongst rural populations and those discharged to a non-home location. To fully understand this complex problem, further investigation using a larger database may be indicated.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging vs computed tomography for baseline imaging evaluation in acute basilar artery occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear. METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality. The primary outcome was mRS 0-3 at 90 days. The secondary outcomes included mRS score shift on an ordinal scale, early neurological deterioration, time from stroke onset to arterial puncture, and time from onset to randomization. The safety outcome was mortality within 90 days. Clinical outcomes and workflow times were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: Among 340 patients (CT: n = 277; MRI: n = 63), baseline imaging was not significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 in the overall cohort (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.50-1.95; P = 0.976). It remained highly consistent across both the endovascular treatment and best medical management subgroups. Baseline MRI assessment was not associated with significant workflow delays compared with CT, including time from stroke onset to randomization (mean difference [MD] 5.23 min; P = 0.843) and time to puncture (MD 13.16 min; P = 0.701). Furthermore, the association between imaging modality and outcomes was consistent across different time windows. DISCUSSION: In patients with acute BAO, we did not observe evidence supporting the preferential use of MRI over CT as the primary imaging strategy for patient selection. Conventional imaging appears sufficient as a first-line tool for selecting patients in clinical practice.

title: MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) Variant Associated With Hereditary Thoracic Aortic Diseases and Early Onset Aortic Dissection.
abstract: AIMS: Thoracic aortic aneurysms and dissections are major causes of sudden cardiovascular death. We aimed to evaluate the clinical significance of the MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) variant in Finnish families with heritable thoracic aortic disease (HTAD) and to assess evidence for a potential founder effect. METHODS: We evaluated the clinical significance and potential founder effect of the missense variant MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) in Finnish families. Eight individuals from four unrelated Finnish families carrying the MYLK c.4079G>A heterozygous variant were recruited. Clinical histories, imaging data, and pedigrees were reviewed. Genetic testing included exome‑based gene panel sequencing or targeted familial variant testing. Variant classification followed the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics 2015 guidelines. RESULTS: Thoracic aortic dilatation or aneurysm occurred in 6/8 carriers (75%), with a mean age at diagnosis of 45 years (range 34-67). Ascending aortic diameters ranged from 26-59 mm, most often measured at the aortic root. Aortic dissection occurred in 4/8 (50%) at a mean age of 46 years (range 34-68), including three early‑adult events. Extrathoracic arterial involvement (carotid) was observed in one variant‑positive individual. CONCLUSION: The MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) variant was present in six affected individuals from four unrelated families and is enriched in the Finnish population, supporting a founder effect. The MYLK c.4079G>A, p.(Gly1360Asp) variant is associated with early‑adult‑onset, high‑penetrance thoracic aortic disease and substantial dissection risk, underscoring the need for vigilant surveillance and early intervention in affected individuals and at‑risk relatives.

title: Reported items and methods for analysis in diagnostic management studies evaluating venous thromboembolism: a systematic review: Communication from the ISTH SSC Subcommittee on Diagnosis and Prediction in Thrombotic Disease.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Reporting of venous thromboembolism (VTE) diagnostic management studies is not standardized, which contributes to incomplete and variable description of study methods and results. This variability hampers interpretation and appraisal of study results. The aim of this study was to evaluate the reporting of key methodology items in recent VTE diagnostic management studies. METHODS: st th A systematic search was conducted in Embase and MEDLINE from January 1, 2005, to August 6, 2024, to identify prospective diagnostic management studies that included adult patients with suspected VTE with follow-up of patients in whom VTE was excluded at baseline. The primary outcome was the reporting of predefined study items. Secondary outcomes were definitions and analysis of diagnostic failure rates and efficiency. RESULTS: Fifty-nine studies were included. Reporting varied: study design, inclusion criteria, follow-up and overall VTE prevalence were consistently reported, whereas location of confirmed PE and reasons for loss to follow-up were poorly reported. Fifty-four studies (92%) reported a definition of the diagnostic failure rate, of which 45 (83%) defined it as the incidence of VTE in all patients in whom VTE had been excluded at baseline. Predefined upper safety margin for the diagnostic failure rate was reported in 34 studies (63%), and varied widely, ranging between 1.5% and 8.0%. Only 8 studies (14%) defined diagnostic efficiency. CONCLUSION: Reporting of key study items, as well as definitions and analysis of diagnostic failure rates varied among VTE diagnostic management studies. Standardization of the reporting and analysis of VTE diagnostic management studies is needed.

title: Incidence of thrombosis and bleeding in patients with JAK2- positive myeloproliferative neoplasms receiving low-dose aspirin: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with JAK2V617F-positive myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are at increased thrombotic risk and commonly receive low-dose aspirin, yet its net clinical benefit is uncertain. OBJECTIVES: We estimated the incidence of thrombotic and bleeding events in patients with JAK2-positive MPNs treated with low-dose aspirin. METHODS: A systematic review was performed for studies evaluating thrombotic and hemorrhagic events in patients with JAK2V617F-positive MPNs while taking low-dose aspirin. Study-level incidence rates (IR) per 100 person-years (PY) and incidence rate ratios (IRR) comparing aspirin use versus no aspirin were calculated and pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 We included 3 randomized clinical trials and 7 observational studies (n=1,760 with aspirin, n=367 without aspirin). The pooled IR of thrombotic events in JAK2V617F-positive MPN patients receiving low-dose aspirin prophylaxis was 2.72 per 100 PY (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.59 - 4.65; I=93%) with pooled IRR receiving aspirin versus no aspirin of 0.59 (95% CI 0.40 - 0.86, I=16%). The pooled IR of major and non-major bleeding on low-dose aspirin prophylaxis was 1.97 (95% CI 1.06 - 3.65; I=90%) per 100 PY with pooled IRR of 2.43 (95% CI 1.15 - 5.11; I=43%). The GRADE level of confidence for the investigated risks was low. CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin was associated with a 40% reduction in thrombosis but a 2.5-fold increase in bleeding risk with low certainty of evidence. More studies are needed to gain high-quality evidence the better define the role of aspirin in JAK2V617F-positive MPNs.

title: Sex-related differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes of ischemic stroke following thrombectomy: data from an inverse propensity score weighted analysis.
abstract: PURPOSE: We investigated sex differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes among ischemic stroke patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT) within 24 h from last known well. METHODS: Consecutive stroke patients who underwent a multimodal CT study protocol, EVT, and non-contrast CT follow-up imaging at 24 h were analyzed. We compared clinical and safety outcomes between males and females who received EVT in both the original population and a Propensity Score-balanced set. We performed univariable analyses to identify baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes that differed between sexes. We used multivariable logistic regression to assess whether sex was associated with outcomes after adjusting for covariates. RESULTS: Among 615 patients included in the analysis, 318 (51.7%) were female. Compared to females, males were younger (p <0.001), more independent before stroke (p <0.001), had a lower prevalence of atrial fibrillation (p < 0.001), and had lower internal carotid artery occlusion (p < 0.013). Compared to male, females had lower total hypoperfused tissue (109.3 mL [IQR=66.4-151.3] vs. 86.3 mL [IQR=43.4-132.3]; p<0.001), lower penumbra volumes (78.1 mL [IQR=43.9-114.8] vs. 47.7 mL [IQR=24.6-76.6], p<0.001), lower mismatch ratio (2.63 [IQR=1.86-4.49] vs. 3.67 [IQR=2.27-6.53]; p<0.001), and lower hypoperfusion intensity ratio (0.30 [IQR=0.18-0.50] vs. 0.38 [IQR=0.22-0.50]; p<0.001). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, sex was not an independent predictor of good clinical outcomes after EVT, although females died less than males and had a lower incidence of hemorrhagic transformation. CONCLUSION: In our cohort of acute ischemic stroke treated with EVT, females showed an overall better perfusion profile at baseline compared to males, suggesting they may be slow progressors; however, this did not translate into better clinical outcomes. More data are needed to clarify the relationship between neuroimaging and sex, as well as the influence of other clinical factors on outcomes among patients undergoing EVT.

title: A multi-stage multimodal learning model for functional outcomes prediction in acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: Predicting functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remains challenging due to the complex and dynamic nature of disease progression. Existing methods typically rely on single-stage imaging or limited multimodal fusion, failing to fully capture disease progression and cross-modal complementarity. To address this issue, we propose a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates multi-stage imaging and clinical notes for 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) prediction. The proposed model leverages a shared foundation model with Low-Rank Adaptation to encode pre- and post-treatment images. It further introduces a shared feature extraction module and a stage-specific feature extraction module to disentangle shared and stage-specific representations, enabling effective modeling of disease progression across stages. In addition, a bidirectional cross-attention module is employed to enhance semantic alignment between imaging features and clinical notes. Experiments on multi-stage NCCT and MRI datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms single-modality baselines, achieving AUCs of 0.9147 and 0.9479, respectively. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of both the multi-stage interaction design and the multimodal fusion strategy. These results suggest that integrating pre- and post-treatment imaging with clinical notes can improve prognostic performance, providing a practical solution for individualized outcome prediction in AIS patients following EVT.

title: Retrieval of Thrombosed Inferior Vena Cava Filter and Mechanical Thrombectomy of Associated Caval Thrombosis Using FlowTriever and ClotTriever Systems With the ClotTriever as Embolic Protection.
abstract: A 55-year-old Chinese male with anti-phospholipid syndrome presented with left lower limb deep venous thrombosis (DVT) on warfarin and had an inferior vena cava filter (IVCF) implanted before a radical resection of a perineal sarcoma. The inferior vena cava (IVC) filter removal was attempted 2 weeks after the surgery, but thrombus was found at the filter. It was decided to leave the filter and to continue with anticoagulation. He presented with progressive right lower limb swelling, erythema and pain, with a CT venogram showing caval thrombosis extending from the IVC filter to the right below-knee veins. In view of worsening symptoms, endovenous mechanical thrombectomy of the IVC and iliofemoral veins, as well as caval filter removal, was performed using the ClotTriever and FlowTriever devices (Inari Medical, US). The ClotTriever itself was then placed alongside a 16Fr internal jugular vein (IJV) sheath to remove the thrombosed filter. The FlowTriever disc was next deployed from jugular access as proximal embolic protection during the thrombectomy procedure. The procedure was successful with no symptoms of pulmonary embolism (PE). This report illustrates the alternative use of the ClotTriever BOLD as an intra-operative proximal embolic protection in the absence of alternative devices like a ProTrieve sheath, during caval thrombectomy and removal for caval thrombosis secondary to an IVC filter.Clinical ImpactThe ClotTriever BOLD catheter, deployed alongside a large retrograde sheath may be considered as an proximal embolic protection for removing thrombosed IVCFs, where there is patient with a suitably sized IVC and when alternative and appropriate devices are unavailable.

title: Impact of Insurance Type on Timing of Diagnosis and Surgical Treatment of Acute Achilles Tendon Ruptures: A 2-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: III Introduction/PurposeDelayed treatment of acute Achilles tendon rupture is associated with worse outcomes and higher complication rates. Prior studies suggest reduced access to care among Medicaid and uninsured patients. This study examines the effect of insurance status on the timing of diagnosis and surgical treatment among patients undergoing surgical repair of acute Achilles tendon rupture.MethodsA retrospective chart review was conducted of patients aged ≥18 years with acute traumatic Achilles tendon ruptures identified by Current Procedural Terminology codes 27650 and 27654 at 2 hospitals between January 2017 and December 2023. Dates of injury, emergency department presentation, initial outpatient orthopaedic evaluation, and surgical intervention were recorded. Only patients who ultimately underwent operative repair were eligible for inclusion; because case ascertainment relied on surgical procedure codes, the cohort does not capture patients managed nonoperatively or those who never reached surgical care. Insurance status was categorized as private or Medicaid/uninsured. Postoperative complications, including re-rupture, infection, venous thromboembolism, wound dehiscence, return to the operating room, and mortality, were documented. Between-group comparisons of continuous variables were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test, given non-normal distribution of the underlying data; independent 2-tailed t-tests were performed as a secondary, confirmatory analysis. Significance was set at P < .05.ResultsThirty-eight surgically treated patients met the inclusion criteria, including 23 with private insurance and 15 who were Medicaid or uninsured. Median age was 35.2 years, and 89.5% were male. All time intervals are reported as medians. Time from injury to emergency department presentation was longer in the Medicaid/uninsured group but not statistically significant (1.0 vs 0.0 days; Mann-Whitney U P = .079). Medicaid/uninsured patients experienced significantly longer delays from injury to initial outpatient orthopaedic evaluation (17.0 vs 4.0 days; Mann-Whitney U P = .024) and from injury to surgery (30.0 vs 10.0 days; Mann-Whitney U P = .045). Time from orthopaedic evaluation to surgery did not differ significantly between groups (11.0 vs 6.0 days; Mann-Whitney U P = .206). Postoperative complications were infrequent in both groups; the study was not powered for comparison of complication rates and none was performed.ConclusionAmong surgically treated patients, those with Medicaid or no insurance experienced significantly longer delays to initial orthopaedic evaluation and to surgical repair compared with privately insured patients, highlighting disparities in access to timely orthopaedic care within this surgically treated population.Level of Evidence:.

title: Taohong Siwu Decoction-Based Targeted Drug Penetration Therapy for Deep Vein Thrombosis After Hip Fracture Surgery: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: Postoperative lower limb deep vein thrombosis (DVT) remains a common complication after hip fracture surgery, and complementary strategies targeting coagulation, inflammation, and venous circulation may provide additional preventive benefits. This retrospective cohort study included 86 patients who underwent hip fracture surgery between June 2023 and June 2024. Patients were assigned to a control group (n = 43), receiving standard low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) prophylaxis, or an observation group (n = 43), receiving additional Taohong Siwu Decoction-based targeted drug penetration therapy. The primary outcome was postoperative lower limb DVT within 10 days after surgery. Secondary outcomes included coagulation parameters, inflammatory markers, femoral venous blood flow velocities, postoperative pain, limb swelling, and treatment-related adverse events. DVT occurred in 1/43 patients (2.33%) in the observation group and 10/43 patients (23.26%) in the control group (Fisher's exact P = 0.007). In a parsimonious Firth penalized logistic regression model adjusting for age and baseline D-dimer, adjunctive therapy remained associated with a lower likelihood of postoperative DVT (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 0.12, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.02-0.68, P = 0.017). After 10 days of treatment, the observation group had lower Faces Pain Scale-Revised scores and limb swelling, longer activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time, lower D-dimer levels, higher common and superficial femoral vein blood flow velocities, and lower serum tumor necrosis factor-alpha and interleukin-6 levels than the control group (all P < 0.05). No statistically significant between-group difference was observed in overall adverse-event occurrence, and no severe treatment-related adverse events were recorded. Taohong Siwu Decoction-based targeted drug penetration therapy combined with standard anticoagulation was associated with a lower incidence of early postoperative DVT and favorable differences in coagulation, inflammatory, and venous hemodynamic parameters.

title: Comparative outcomes of arteriovenous accesses with and without tunneled hemodialysis catheters: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: This study compared patency rates of arteriovenous accesses with and without concurrent tunneled hemodialysis catheter (THC) use, addressing limited research on combined outcomes. A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted on patients undergoing arteriovenous access creation at a single hospital between January 2021 and December 2022. Primary outcomes were the 6-month primary patency rate and functional dialysis success. Secondary outcomes were the factors associated with each of these endpoints. Statistical analyses employed t tests, chi-square tests, logistic regression, and Kaplan-Meier survival curves. A total of 319 vascular accesses were included. The 6-month patency rate was significantly higher in the access-only group than in the access + THC group (87.04% vs 78.20%, P = .04). THC usage (odds ratio [OR] = 0.49, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.25-0.95, P = .03), graft usage (OR = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.18-0.82, P = .01), and higher hemoglobin levels (OR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.65-0.96, P = .02) were associated with reduced patency rates. Functional dialysis success at 6 months did not differ significantly between groups (87.96% vs 83.89%, P = .21). However, older age (OR = 0.96, 95% CI: 0.93-0.99, P = .01), use of a cubital artery to an autologous vein (OR = 0.39, 95% CI: 0.19-0.82, P = .01) or graft (OR = 0.40, 95% CI: 0.17-0.97, P = .04), and higher hemoglobin levels (OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.66-0.99, P = .03) were associated with a lower likelihood of functional dialysis success. Concurrent THC use was independently associated with reduced 6-month primary patency without a corresponding reduction in the short-term delivery of dialysis, suggesting an increased need for interventions to maintain the access. Judicious use of THCs and careful consideration of the vascular access type are important to optimize vascular access outcomes in patients undergoing hemodialysis.
